lessons.title: Kazanmak, harcamak, biriktirmek
lessons.goal: Parayla ilgili fiilleri ve kelime eşlemelerini doğal bir şekilde kullanabilirim.

lines.speaker: Barış

learn.explanation:
**Sık karıştırılan para fiilleri:**

| Fiil | Anlam | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **borrow** (from) | ödünç **almak** | I **borrowed** 100 lira **from** my sister. |
| **lend** (to) | ödünç **vermek** | My sister **lent** me 100 lira. |
| **owe** | borçlu olmak | I **owe** her 100 lira. |
| **pay back** | borcu geri ödemek | I'll **pay** you **back** on Friday. |
| **earn** | (çalışarak) kazanmak | She **earns** 40,000 a month. |
| **win** | (yarışma/şans) kazanmak | He **won** the lottery. |
| **afford** | parası yetmek | I **can't afford** it. |

**Doğal kelime eşlemeleri (collocations):**

| Fiil | + isim |
|---|---|
| **make** | money, a profit, a loss, a living |
| **save** | money, time / **save up for** a car |
| **spend** | money **on** sth, time |
| **waste** | money **on** sth, time |
| **take out** | a loan, a mortgage (konut kredisi) |
| **pay off** | a loan, a debt |
| **get into / get out of** | debt |
| **live on** | a low income, 20,000 a month |

**Dikkat:** ~~earn money from the lottery~~ → **win** money. / ~~make a budget~~ ve **set a budget** ikisi de kullanılır.

examples.en: They took out a loan to start a business.
It's hard to live on a student budget.

"Can you borrow me some money?" yanlıştır; doğrusu "Can you lend me some money?" ya da "Can I borrow some money?". Ayrıca "kazanmak" İngilizcede earn (çalışarak), win (yarışma) ve make (para kazanmak, kâr etmek) olarak ayrılır.

lessons.title: Endişe verici mi, endişeli mi?
lessons.goal: -ing ve -ed sıfatlarını (worrying / worried, shocking / shocked) doğru ve çeşitli kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Bir ekonomi blogundan
discover.body:
This month's figures are worrying. Food prices have risen again, and many families are worried about how they will pay their bills this winter.

What's surprising is that, at the same time, sales of luxury goods have increased. Economists aren't surprised, though. They say it's a sign that the gap between rich and poor is getting wider, which is alarming.

There is some encouraging news, however. Unemployment has fallen slightly, and young people who are interested in technology are finding jobs more easily.

It's frustrating for many people to work hard and still struggle to save money. But experts say that small changes in our spending habits can make an amazing difference over time.

questions.prompt: Why aren't economists surprised by luxury sales?
options: It shows the gap between rich and poor is growing.
questions.explanation: "a sign that the gap between rich and poor is getting wider"

learn.explanation:
Bu iki sıfat türünü A2'den beri biliyorsunuz (*bored / boring*). B2'de daha geniş bir kelime yelpazesi ve daha ince kullanımlar öğreniyoruz.

| -ing (sebep: şey/durum **nasıl**) | -ed (sonuç: kişi **ne hissediyor**) |
|---|---|
| The news is **worrying**. | People are **worried**. |
| The price was **shocking**. | I was **shocked**. |
| The result was **disappointing**. | We were **disappointed**. |
| It's **frustrating**. | I feel **frustrated**. |
| The rise is **alarming**. | Experts are **alarmed**. |
| The figures are **encouraging**. | We feel **encouraged**. |
| The offer was **tempting**. | I was **tempted** to buy it. |
| It's **overwhelming**. | I felt **overwhelmed**. |

**Önemli:** Bir **kişi** de -ing sıfatıyla anlatılabilir: o zaman o kişinin **başkalarında yarattığı etki** anlatılır.

- *He's **boring**.* (Sıkıcı biri; başkalarını sıkar.)
- *He's **bored**.* (Canı sıkılıyor.)
- *My boss is very **demanding**.* (Çok şey bekleyen, zorlayıcı biri.)

**Edatlar:** worried **about**, disappointed **with/by/in**, shocked **by/at**, interested **in**, tempted **to** + fiil

examples.en: The rise in rents is alarming.
I was tempted to buy it, but it was too expensive.
examples.tr: Almaya can attı ama çok pahalıydı.

examples.en: Dealing with debt can be overwhelming.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "endişe verici" ve "endişeli", "sıkıcı" ve "sıkılmış" farklı ekler alır; İngilizcede bu ayrım -ing ve -ed ile yapılır. Türkçe konuşanların B2'de bile sık yaptığı hata "I'm boring" (Ben sıkıcıyım) demektir, oysa kastedilen "I'm bored" (Canım sıkılıyor). Kural basit: -ed bir duygu, -ing o duyguya neden olan şey.

options: Çok şey talep eden, zorlayıcı biri
I was tempting to buy it.
I was tempted to buy it.

task.prompt: Ekonomi ya da kendi finansal durumunuzla ilgili son zamanlarda sizi etkileyen 5 şeyi anlatın. Her biri için hem -ing hem -ed sıfatı kullanın: worrying / worried, shocking / shocked, frustrating / frustrated, encouraging / encouraged, tempting / tempted, overwhelming / overwhelmed.
task.modelAnswer: The rise in rents in my city is shocking. I was shocked when my landlord asked for 30% more. It's also frustrating that my salary hasn't gone up, so I feel frustrated every time I pay the bills. Online sales are really tempting, and I'm often tempted to buy things I don't need. On the other hand, my savings plan is going well, which is encouraging. Planning everything can be overwhelming, but I feel less worried now that I have a budget.

lessons.title: Ekonominin dili
lessons.goal: Ekonomi haberlerinde sık geçen sıfat + isim ve isim + isim collocation'larını anlayabilir ve kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Haber özeti: Ekonomide bu hafta
discover.body:
The central bank announced on Thursday that it would keep interest rates unchanged for the third month in a row.

Inflation remains high, and the rising cost of living continues to put pressure on households. Many families are spending a larger share of their income on basic needs such as food and housing.

Meanwhile, the job market is showing signs of improvement. The unemployment rate fell slightly, and several companies have announced plans to create new jobs in the technology sector.

Experts warn, however, that economic growth is likely to remain slow next year. Small businesses, in particular, are struggling with high energy costs and fierce competition from online shops.

questions.prompt: What did the central bank do?
What are small businesses struggling with?
options: High energy costs and competition from online shops

learn.explanation:
Ekonomi dilinde bazı kelimeler **belli kelimelerle** birlikte kullanılır. Bunları **kalıp olarak** öğrenin.

**Sıfat + isim:**

| Doğal | Doğal değil |
|---|---|
| **high / low** inflation | ~~big~~ inflation |
| **high / low** prices | ~~expensive~~ prices |
| **fierce / strong** competition | ~~hard~~ competition |
| **steady / slow / rapid** growth | ~~fast~~ growth (kullanılır ama az) |
| a **tight** budget | ~~narrow~~ budget |
| a **low / high** income | ~~small~~ income |
| a **heavy** debt / **heavily** in debt | ~~big~~ debt |

**İsim + isim:**

- **interest** rate, **unemployment** rate, **exchange** rate (döviz kuru)
- **job** market, **housing** market, **stock** market
- **cost** of living, **standard** of living
- **energy** costs, **living** costs

**Fiil + isim:**

- **create** jobs, **cut** taxes / costs, **raise** prices / taxes / interest rates
- **put pressure on** sb, **struggle with** costs

**Dikkat:** ***prices*** **high / low** olur, **expensive / cheap** olmaz. *Products* expensive olur.

- ~~The prices are expensive.~~ → **Prices are high.** / **Things are expensive.**

examples.en: Inflation has remained high this year.
Small shops face fierce competition from online retailers.
examples.tr: Küçük dükkânlar çevrimiçi satıcılardan gelen sert rekabetle karşı karşıya.

examples.en: The government plans to create 100,000 new jobs.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "fiyatlar pahalı" demek doğal gelir; İngilizcede ise "prices are expensive" yanlış bir eşleşmedir: prices are high, things are expensive. Benzer şekilde "büyük enflasyon" değil "high inflation", "sıkı bütçe" değil "tight budget" deyin. Collocation'lar sözlükte tek tek bulunmaz; okuyarak ve not alarak öğrenilir.

lessons.title: Grafiği anlatmak
lessons.goal: Fiyatlardaki ve rakamlardaki değişimleri fiil + zarf ve sıfat + isim yapılarıyla doğru betimleyebilirim.

discover.title: Bir kafenin yıllık raporu
discover.body:
The chart shows the monthly income of a small café in Eskişehir last year.

In January, income was quite low, at around 80,000 lira. It rose steadily in the spring and reached 120,000 in May.

In June, there was a sharp rise, as students finished their exams and tourists began to arrive. Income peaked at 180,000 lira in August.

In September, income fell dramatically when the summer season ended, but it then remained stable at about 110,000 for the rest of the autumn.

In December, there was a slight increase because of the holidays. Overall, the café's income almost doubled between January and August.

learn.explanation:
**Değişimi anlatmanın iki yolu:**

| Fiil + zarf | Sıfat + isim |
|---|---|
| Prices **rose sharply**. | There was **a sharp rise** in prices. |
| Sales **fell slightly**. | There was **a slight fall** in sales. |
| Income **increased steadily**. | There was **a steady increase** in income. |
| Costs **dropped dramatically**. | There was **a dramatic drop** in costs. |

**Fiiller:**

| Yukarı ↗ | Aşağı ↘ | Sabit → | Zirve / dip |
|---|---|---|---|
| rise, increase, go up, grow | fall, decrease, go down, drop, decline | remain stable, stay the same, level off | peak (at), reach a peak, hit a low |
| double (iki katına çıkmak) | halve (yarıya inmek) | | |

**Zarflar / sıfatlar (hıza ve miktara göre):**

- **Büyük:** sharply / sharp, dramatically / dramatic, significantly / significant
- **Orta:** steadily / steady, gradually / gradual
- **Küçük:** slightly / slight

**Edatlar çok önemli:**

- rose **from** 80,000 **to** 120,000
- rose **by** 40,000 (fark)
- peaked **at** 180,000
- a rise **in** prices / a rise **of** 20%

examples.en: The price of bread rose by 15% last year.
There was a sharp fall in sales in January.
examples.tr: Ocak ayında satışlarda keskin bir düşüş oldu.

examples.en: Unemployment peaked at 12% and then fell gradually.
examples.tr: İşsizlik %12 ile zirveye ulaştı, sonra yavaş yavaş düştü.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "%15 arttı" derken edat kullanılmaz; İngilizcede "rose by 15%" (fark) ile "rose to 15%" (ulaşılan değer) çok farklı anlamlara gelir. "Enflasyon %5 arttı" cümlesinin İngilizcesi bağlama göre "rose by 5%" ya da "rose to 5%" olur. Grafik betimlerken by, to, from ve at'e çok dikkat edin.

practice.text: Sales peaked ___ 2 million in July.
There was a slight ___ in prices. (düşüş)
Income increased ___ (steady) throughout the year.
After the summer, the number of visitors remained ___. (sabit)

task.prompt: Son bir yılda sizin için önemli bir şeyin değişimini bir grafik anlatır gibi betimleyin: kiranız, bir ürünün fiyatı, aylık harcamalarınız, telefonunuzda geçirdiğiniz süre, vb. En az 3 fiil + zarf, 2 sıfat + isim yapısı kullanın ve from / to / by / at edatlarını doğru kullanın.
task.modelAnswer: I'd like to describe how my monthly spending on food changed last year. In January, I was spending about 6,000 lira a month. It rose steadily in the spring and reached 8,000 in May. In the summer, there was a sharp increase because I ate out a lot on holiday, and it peaked at 11,000 in August. In September, it fell dramatically when I started cooking at home again. It then remained stable at around 7,500. Overall, my spending rose by about 25% over the year.

lessons.title: Para tavsiyesi
lessons.goal: Ünitedeki kelime ve yapıları kullanarak gençlere kişisel finans tavsiyesi veren ikna edici bir blog yazısı yazabilirim.

discover.title: Blog: İlk maaşınla yapman gereken 5 şey
discover.body:
Congratulations on your first job! It's an exciting moment, and it's tempting to spend your first salary on something special. But a few smart decisions now can save you a lot of stress later.

1. Make a budget. Write down your monthly income and expenses. You might be shocked by how much you spend on coffee and takeaways.

2. Pay yourself first. As soon as you get paid, put at least 10% into a savings account. If you wait until the end of the month, there will be nothing left.

3. Build an emergency fund. Try to save enough to cover three months of living costs. It will make unexpected bills much less frightening.

4. Avoid debt if you can. Credit cards are convenient, but the interest rates are often very high. Never borrow money to buy things you don't really need.

5. Treat yourself, but wisely. You've earned it! Just make sure it's worth the money.

Managing money isn't always exciting, but feeling in control of your finances is one of the most satisfying feelings in the world.

options: Put money into savings as soon as you get paid.
questions.explanation: "put at least 10% into a savings account"

questions.prompt: How much should an emergency fund cover?

learn.explanation:
**Tavsiye veren blog yazısının özellikleri:**

| Özellik | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **Okuyucuya doğrudan hitap** | *Congratulations on your first job!* / *You might be shocked ...* |
| **Numaralı başlıklar** | *1. Make a budget.* (emir kipiyle kısa başlıklar) |
| **Gerekçe** | *If you wait ..., there will be nothing left.* (koşul cümlesi) |
| **Çeşitli tavsiye kalıpları** | *Try to ... / Make sure ... / Avoid + -ing / Never ... / It's a good idea to ... / You should ...* |
| **Duyguya hitap** (-ing / -ed sıfatlar) | *exciting, tempting, frightening, satisfying* |
| **Güçlü kapanış** | Bir özet ya da motive edici bir cümle |

**Tavsiye kalıpları:**

- ***Make sure** you read the small print.* (Mutlaka ... )
- ***Avoid** taking out loans for holidays.* (avoid + **-ing**)
- ***It's worth** comparing prices.* (worth + **-ing**)
- ***The key is to** start early.*
- ***If I were you, I'd** ...*

**Üslup:** Blog yazısı **yarı samimi**dir: kısaltmalar (*you'll, don't*) ve doğrudan hitap kullanılır, ama dil düzgün ve açıktır.

examples.en: Make sure you compare prices before you buy.
Avoid using your credit card for everyday shopping.
examples.tr: Günlük alışverişlerde kredi kartı kullanmaktan kaçın.

examples.en: It's worth setting up an automatic savings plan.
examples.tr: Otomatik bir birikim planı kurmaya değer.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe blog yazılarında tavsiyeler genellikle "-malısınız" ile verilir ve tekrar edilir. İngilizcede "You should" yerine çeşitli kalıplar kullanmak (Make sure, Avoid, It's worth, Try to) yazıyı çok daha canlı yapar. "avoid" ve "worth" kelimelerinden sonra -ing geldiğini unutmayın: "Avoid to spend" yanlıştır, "Avoid spending" doğrudur.

task.prompt: Üniversite öğrencilerine yönelik bir blog için "Öğrenci bütçesiyle nasıl geçinilir?" konulu bir yazı yazın (180–220 kelime). İlgi çekici bir girişle başlayın, numaralı en az 4 tavsiye verin ve her birini gerekçelendirin. En az 6 para collocation'ı (live on, cut back on, save up for, a tight budget, can't afford, waste money on), en az 3 -ing / -ed sıfat ve çeşitli tavsiye kalıpları (Make sure, Avoid + -ing, It's worth + -ing) kullanın.
task.modelAnswer:
Living on a student budget: 5 tips that actually work

Let's be honest: being a student is exciting, but living on a tight budget can be really stressful. Here are five tips that helped me survive my first year without getting into debt.

1. Track every lira. For one month, write down everything you spend. Most students are shocked to see how much they waste on snacks and coffee.

2. Cook in groups. Takeaways are tempting after a long day, but they're expensive. Cooking with your flatmates is cheaper, healthier and more fun.

3. Use your student card. It's worth asking for a student discount everywhere: cinemas, museums, public transport and even some cafés.

4. Avoid buying new textbooks. Second-hand books or library copies are just as good, and you can sell them again at the end of the year.

5. Save up for the things you really want. If you can't afford something now, put a small amount aside each week. Make sure you never borrow money for things you don't need.

Cutting back on spending isn't always fun, but the feeling of reaching the end of the month with money in your account is incredibly satisfying. Trust me, it's worth it!

Can you lend me some money?

questions.prompt: "Okullarda finansal okuryazarlık dersi zorunlu olmalı mı?" sorusuna bir blog yazısıyla cevap verin (180–220 kelime). Görüşünüzü belirtin, en az 3 gerekçe verin, bir karşı görüşe değinin ve güçlü bir kapanış yapın. Para collocation'ları, -ing / -ed sıfatlar, en az bir eğilim betimlemesi (rose sharply / a steady increase) ve tavsiye kalıpları kullanın.
questions.modelAnswer:
Should every school teach money?

Most of us leave school knowing how to solve equations, but very few of us know how to make a budget, how interest rates work or what happens when you can't pay off a credit card. In my opinion, financial education should be compulsory in every secondary school.

First, young people are getting into debt earlier than ever. Among my own friends, the number of people with credit card debt has risen sharply since we started university. Many of them simply don't understand how quickly interest can grow.

Second, the cost of living has increased steadily, and good money habits are now more important than ever. Learning to save, to compare prices and to avoid wasting money on things you don't need is a skill for life.

Finally, money is a common source of stress. Studies suggest that people who feel in control of their finances are less worried and more satisfied with their lives.

Some people argue that parents, not schools, should teach children about money. That's a fair point, but not every parent has the knowledge or the time to do it.

It's worth remembering that almost every adult decision involves money. Surely it's time our schools prepared students for that.
